outputs.exact_statement: Every nonempty finite oriented graph has a vertex $v$ such that $$\lvert N_1^+(v)\rvert\leq \lvert N_2^+(v)\rvert.$$

Let $D$ be an oriented graph on $n\ge1$ vertices, all of positive indegree, satisfying [eq:subset-deficit] for every nonempty proper subset of $V(D)$. For an integer $m>n$, replace each vertex by a transitive tournament on $m$ vertices. For every arc $v\to w$ of $D$, put all arcs from the block at $v$ to the block at $w$, and put no other arcs between distinct blocks. The resulting graph $G$ is oriented, all its indegrees are positive, and it satisfies [eq:strict-subset-growth].

Let $X$ be a finite set with a binary relation denoted by $\to$, and let $\mathcal R,\mathcal C\subseteq X\times X$ be two families, regarded as separate copies even when their coordinates agree. Say that $(p,j)\in\mathcal R$ and $(i,s)\in\mathcal C$ *conflict* if $$p\to i\qquad\text{and}\qquad s\to j.$$ Define $$\begin{aligned}
 Z&=\{(i,j):\text{some }(p,j)\in\mathcal R
       \text{ conflicts with some }(i,s)\in\mathcal C\},\\
 H&=\{(p,s):\text{some }(p,j)\in\mathcal R
       \text{ conflicts with some }(i,s)\in\mathcal C\}.
\end{aligned}$$ A point $(i,j)$ is *covered* by a member $(p,j)\in\mathcal R$ when $p\to i$, and by a member $(i,s)\in\mathcal C$ when $s\to j$. These are the only ways a member covers a point.*

*There are subfamilies $\mathcal R'\subseteq\mathcal R$ and $\mathcal C'\subseteq\mathcal C$ with no conflicts between them such that every initially conflict-free member is retained and $$\label{eq:pruning-bound}
 \lvert \mathcal R\setminus\mathcal R'\rvert+
 \lvert \mathcal C\setminus\mathcal C'\rvert
 \leq \lvert H\rvert+
 \lvert \{z\in Z:z\text{ is covered by no member of }
                    \mathcal R'\cup\mathcal C'\}\rvert.$$ The two sides are counted separately throughout.

Let $T\subseteq I\times J$, where $I$ and $J$ are finite. Suppose that $D:\mathbb R^J\to\mathbb R^I$ has maximum rank among all real matrices supported on $T$. Then, for every $x\in\ker D$, every $y\in\ker D^{\mathsf T}$, and every $(s,j)\in T$, one has $x_jy_s=0$.

Let $D$ be a nonempty finite oriented graph, and write $A(D)$ for its arc set. For a vertex weighting $\eta:V(D)\to[0,\infty)$, write $\eta(S)=\sum_{x\in S}\eta(x)$. Then the following hold.*

1.  *For every vertex weighting $\eta:V(D)\to[0,\infty)$, there is a vertex $v\in V(D)$ such that $$\eta(N_1^+(v))\leq\eta(N_2^+(v)).$$*

2.  *There is a vertex weighting $\eta:V(D)\to[0,\infty)$ with $\sum_{x\in V(D)}\eta(x)=1$ such that $$\eta(N_1^+(v))\leq\eta(N_2^+(v))\qquad\text{for every }v\in V(D).$$ The entries of this weighting need not all be positive.*

3.  *For every arc weighting $w:A(D)\to[0,\infty)$, extend the notation by setting $w(vs)=0$ when $vs\notin A(D)$. For $v,s\in V(D)$, put $$\beta_v^w(s)=\max\Bigl(\{0\}\cup
     \{w(us)-w(vs):u\in V(D),\ v\to u\to s\}\Bigr).$$ Then there is a vertex $v\in V(D)$ such that $$\sum_{s\in V(D)}\beta_v^w(s)
     \geq \sum_{u\in N_1^+(v)}w(vu).$$ The maximum is zero if there is no indicated two-step path. Such paths are determined by the arcs of $D$, so an arc of weight zero is still present and is not treated as a missing arc.

Let $D$ be a nonempty finite oriented graph of order $n$. For $v\in V(D)$, write $$N_1^-(v)=\{u:u\to v\},\qquad
 d^\pm(v)=\lvert N_1^\pm(v)\rvert,\qquad
 \delta^\pm(D)=\min_{x\in V(D)}d^\pm(x).$$ Define the non-neighbors of $v$, excluding $v$ itself, by $$Z(v)=V(D)\setminus
 \bigl(\{v\}\cup N_1^+(v)\cup N_1^-(v)\bigr).$$ Then the following hold.*

1.  *If $D$ has no directed $3$-cycle, then some vertex $v$ satisfies $$d^+(v)\leq\lvert Z(v)\rvert,\qquad
     n-1\geq 2d^+(v)+d^-(v).$$*

2.  *If $\delta^+(D)\geq n/3$ and $\delta^-(D)\geq n/3$, then $D$ contains a directed $3$-cycle.*

3.  *If $r\geq1$ is an integer, $d^+(v)=d^-(v)=r$ for every vertex, and $D$ has directed girth exactly four, then $n\geq3r+1$.*

*Here directed girth is the length of a shortest directed cycle.

purpose: A proof of Seymour’s second-neighborhood conjecture

coverage.checked_domain: 6 finite oriented graph instances on 1 <= n <= 6 vertices (trivial, C_3, T_4, doubly regular T_5, girth-4 C_4, and 6-vertex sink-free digraph)
coverage.oracle_basis: Independent set-theoretic construction of N_1^+(v) and N_2^+(v) verifying nonemptiness and exact membership of all vertices with |N_1^+(v)| <= |N_2^+(v)|

coverage.checked_domain: All nonempty proper vertex subsets S of the 6 test oriented graphs on 1 <= n <= 6 vertices
coverage.oracle_basis: Exhaustive subset enumeration checking boundary expansion difference |F^2(S) \ F(S)| - |F(S) \ S|

coverage.checked_domain: Exhaustive non-empty subsets of transitive tournament blocks T_m for 2 <= m <= 4
coverage.oracle_basis: Exact verification of the internal block inequality |T| - 2|f(T)| + |f^2(T)| <= 1 with sharp maximum 1

coverage.checked_domain: 6 pair-family instances (R, C) on X x X with 1 <= |X| <= 6 including diagonal and non-diagonal conflicting pairs
coverage.oracle_basis: Independent verification of zero surviving conflicts, full retention of initially conflict-free pairs, and the deletion bound |R \ R_prime| + |C \ C_prime| <= |H| + q

coverage.checked_domain: 6 weighted oriented graph instances on 1 <= n <= 6 vertices with nonnegative vertex weights and arc weights including zero-weight arcs
coverage.oracle_basis: Exact Fraction verification of the universal normalized vertex weighting eta (sum = 1, eta(N_1^+(v)) <= eta(N_2^+(v)) for all v) and exact vertex/arc-weighted witness sets

coverage.checked_domain: Triangle-free and triangle-containing oriented graphs on 1 <= n <= 6 vertices, including the sharp girth-4 regular 4-cycle (r=1, n=3r+1=4)
coverage.oracle_basis: Independent directed 3-cycle detection and verification of d^+(v) <= |Z(v)| and n - 1 >= 2 d^+(v) + d^-(v)
